children: Indian shares opened marginally lower on Friday, with the benchmark indexes easing off nine-month highs and overbought conditions, while other Asian markets slid as Anthropic's
debut failed to restore faith in AI trades.
edged 0.19% lower to 82,863.67, as of 9:18 a.m. IST.
Eleven of the 16 major sectors logged losses at the open. The broader small-caps
fell 2%, pressured by concerns over the strength of AI-related demand and a firmer dollar.

Despite the negative open, the Nifty and Sensex are up 1.3% and 1.6% this week, on course for their fourth straight weekly gain, helped by a record $12.21 billion of monthly foreign inflows on AI-trade unwind, easing crude oil prices and upbeat earnings.

Asian markets, on the other hand, are on track for their worst week since 2020. MSCI's broadest index of Asia-Pacific shares (.MISX00000PUS) lost 2.5% on Friday as strong demand for Anthropic shares didn't carry through to gains in shares of AI supply chain companies.
